segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Friends brought a blind man to Jesus in Bethsaida and begged Him just to touch him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus took the man by the hand and walked him outside the village.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He spit on the man's eyes and laid His hands on him, then asked if he could see anything yet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The man looked up and said the strangest thing — he could see, but only halfway. People looked like trees walking around. His first glimpse was real, but unfinished. Jesus did not scold him for saying so.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus put His hands on the man's eyes a second time and told him to look up again.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And this time he saw everything clearly — every face, every leaf. The second touch finished what the first had started. The story never explains why healing came in stages. It simply shows that an unfinished beginning was not the end.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Maybe your faith came in stages too. Partial sight is not proof that he has left. He is patient enough to touch you twice.
